The video linked in the article explains it all. The adverts are usually made before the car design is fully finalized with model tweaks and revisions coming in very late in the process, which they can change in the computer with less trouble than re-shooting the whole ad.

The blackbird stand-in car can also adjust it's suspension and wheelbase to mimic most given cars so the overlaid CGI looks like it's integrated into the environment even more. The cameras on and in the car capture environmental and VR data too.

The blackbird is pretty new as far as I remember, and has probably only been used for 6 months or so, so we've probably seen a few ads using it, but not so many using the actual blackbird. The company that built it has been doing CGI vehicles for ads for years, but they've always had to have a car with a similar size, weight, and suspension so the tracking points seem realistic.

They designed the blackbird to match any car so they can get better matches on the tracking points, and as such much nicer cgi cars in ads.
